real.title: Serving signature silently maps every unrecognized Polars dtype (Decimal/Time/Duration/List/Struct/Binary/Object/Null) to string, producing a wrong serving contract
real.description: `_to_colspecs` builds the MLflow ModelSignature from the resolved input/output schema dicts, whose values are `str(polars_dtype)` strings (see `infer_input_schema`/`infer_output_schema` in src/haute/deploy/_schema.py:71,141). It takes `base_type = dtype_str.split('(')[0]` and then `dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string)`. `dtype_map` only covers integers, floats, String/Utf8, Boolean, Date, Datetime. Any other Polars dtype the pipeline legitimately produces -- `Decimal(...)` (e.g. a premium/money column), `Time`, `Duration`, `List(...)`, `Struct(...)`, `Categorical`, `Enum`, `Binary`, `Null`, `Object` -- has a base name not in the map and is SILENTLY coerced to `DataType.string`. The deployed Databricks Model Serving signature then advertises those columns as string, so the endpoint's input validation/coercion is wrong for those fields (a numeric Decimal column is described as text). This directly contradicts the project's 'fail loudly, no incorrect silent fallbacks' principle, and notably the sibling builder src/haute/modelling/_signature.py RAISES `ValueError('Unknown polars dtype ...')` on the very same dtype families (cataloged finding `signature-build-aborts-mlflow-run-on-temporal-decimal-features`) -- the deploy path takes the opposite, silent-and-wrong behavior. Evidence: `dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string)` at line 244 with no membership check; e.g. `str(pl.Decimal(18,2))` -> 'Decimal(precision=18, scale=2)' -> base 'Decimal' -> not in dtype_map -> DataType.string.
real.evidence: Repro output: "MLflow signature input type map: {'premium': string, 'tod': string, 'elapsed': string, 'tags': string}" and "MLflow signature output type map: {'final_premium': string}". premium dtype str = 'Decimal(precision=18, scale=2)' (base 'Decimal' is absent from dtype_map at _mlflow.py:221-237, so line 244 `dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string)` silently yields DataType.string). The sibling builder raises on the identical string: "Unknown polars dtype 'Decimal(precision=18, scale=2)'. Supported dtypes: ['Boolean', 'Float64', 'Int64', 'String']".
real.fix: In `_to_colspecs` (src/haute/deploy/_mlflow.py:239-246), stop defaulting unknown base types to `DataType.string`. Replace `dtype_map.get(base_type, DataType.string)` with an explicit membership check that raises a clear ValueError on unmapped dtypes (mirroring src/haute/modelling/_signature.py:22-27, e.g. `Unknown polars dtype {dtype_str!r}; supported: {sorted(dtype_map)}`). Optionally add genuine mappings for dtypes the serving path can legitimately support (e.g. Decimal -> DataType.double or a documented numeric choice) rather than coercing money columns to text. As part of the fix, update the now-incorrect test `test_unknown_dtype_falls_back_to_string` (tests/test_deploy_internals.py:3371-3384) to assert the loud ValueError, and add a regression test that a Decimal input/output dtype raises (so the silent-string contract can never reappear). NOTE: the existing test currently encodes the wrong fallback as intended behaviour — it asserts `Unknown dtype must fall back to string` — so it must be changed, not merely left passing.

real.title: Registered model version is re-derived via max(search_versions) instead of the value returned by log_model -- races to the wrong version and silently guesses "1" when the search is empty
real.description: `mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(...)` returns a `ModelInfo` whose `registered_model_version` is the exact version just created (confirmed present in the installed mlflow 3.10.0: `ModelInfo.registered_model_version`). The code discards that return value and instead re-queries ALL versions of the UC model with `search_versions(client, uc_model_name)` and takes `max(versions, key=lambda v: int(v.version)).version`, falling back to the string `"1"` when `versions` is empty. Two defects: (1) Race/shared-state -- if another deploy of the same UC model registers a higher version between this `log_model` call and the `search_versions` call, `max()` returns that OTHER deploy's version, which is then passed as `model_version=int(latest_version)` to `_create_or_update_serving_endpoint` (line 152), so the live serving endpoint is bound to the wrong model version, and the wrong `v{model_version}` is reported to the user (cli/_deploy.py:201). (2) Silent incorrect fallback -- after a SUCCESSFUL `log_model` there is always at least one version; an empty `search_versions` result indicates a genuine registry problem, yet the `else: latest_version = "1"` branch fabricates version 1 and proceeds to serve/return it, masking the failure. This violates the project's 'no incorrect silent fallbacks / fail loudly' rule. Using `log_model(...).registered_model_version` eliminates both the race and the bogus fallback in one line.
real.evidence: Repro output: "[defect1] log_model registered v7; concurrent deploy registered v42 -> DeployResult.model_version=42, served model_version=42, model_uri='models:/ws.default.my-model/42'" and "[defect2] log_model registered v5; search_versions empty -> DeployResult.model_version=1, served model_version=1". Both DeployResult.model_version AND the model_version passed to _create_or_update_serving_endpoint are demonstrably wrong (expected 7 -> got 42; expected 5 -> got 1). Installed mlflow 3.10.0 source confirms the fix is sound: in mlflow.models.model.Model.log, `if registered_model_name is not None: ... model_info.registered_model_version = registered_model.version`, and mlflow.pyfunc.log_model returns that ModelInfo — the value src/haute/deploy/_mlflow.py:124 discards. No downstream guard corrects latest_version; it flows unscoped into model_uri (line 142), endpoint binding (line 151), and DeployResult.model_version (line 163), reported to the user at src/haute/cli/_deploy.py:201.
real.fix: Capture the ModelInfo returned by log_model and use its version directly, eliminating both the race and the bogus fallback in one line. In deploy_to_mlflow: change `mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(...)` (lines 124-131) to `model_info = mlflow.pyfunc.log_model(...)`, then replace the search_versions/max/"1"-fallback block (lines 134-140) with `latest_version = str(model_info.registered_model_version)` and a loud check: `if model_info.registered_model_version is None: raise RuntimeError(f"log_model did not register a version for {uc_model_name}; registry may be misconfigured")`. The MlflowClient/search_versions re-query is then unnecessary for this path. Update tests/test_deploy.py: the mock_mlflow_deploy harness currently leaves log_model's return as a bare MagicMock and forces search_model_versions->[], so test_deploy_calls_create_or_update_endpoint asserting model_version=1 (line 1304) is asserting the buggy fallback — set m_log_model.return_value.registered_model_version to an explicit int and assert on that instead. Add a regression test that returns a higher search_versions value than the log_model version and asserts the served/reported version equals the log_model version.

real.title: liveSwitch deploy pruning MAPPED (input_scenario_map) path silently selects the wrong live branch when two upstream labels collide under _sanitize_func_name (order-dependent, no ambiguity guard)
real.description: When a liveSwitch node DOES have an input_scenario_map with a 'live' entry, _live_only_edges resolves the live edge by scanning the switch's incoming edges and taking the FIRST whose source label sanitizes to live_input_name (lines 59-64), then `break`s. The guard at lines 65-69 only raises when NO edge matches. It does NOT detect the case where TWO distinct upstream source nodes have labels that collide under _sanitize_func_name (e.g. 'Live Source' and 'Live-Source' both -> 'Live_Source', since sanitize maps both space and hyphen to '_'). In that case both edges 'match' live_input_name; whichever edge is listed first in graph.edges wins, the other live-candidate is dropped, and prune_for_deploy returns normally with NO error. The deployed scoring path therefore depends on edge ordering and can keep the WRONG upstream branch. This is the inverse of the already-known fallback finding: the known finding (bucket 'known', verdict refuted) asserts the mapped path is the safe one that 'raises on no-match/collision, unlike the fallback' — this finding shows the mapped path is ALSO silently order-dependent on COLLISION (it only raises on no-match, not on ambiguous-match). It is also distinct from the codegen B3 finding, which concerns two input_scenario_map keys both mapped to 'live' (duplicate map VALUES); here the map has a single 'live' key but two SOURCE LABELS collide after sanitization.
real.evidence: Repro output (exit 0): _sanitize_func_name('Live Source') -> 'Live_Source' and _sanitize_func_name('Live-Source') -> 'Live_Source'; edge_order ('a','b') -> prune_for_deploy no error, surviving switch parent(s) {'a'}, kept ids ['a','output','switch']; edge_order ('b','a') -> no error, surviving switch parent(s) {'b'}, kept ids ['b','output','switch']. The kept live branch flips with edge order, silently. Code trace: src/haute/deploy/_pruner.py L59-64 `for e in edges: if e.target==sid: if _sanitize_func_name(src_label)==live_input_name: switch_live_source[sid]=e.source; break` (first-match-wins), and L65 `if sid not in switch_live_source:` guard only fires on NO match, so a colliding match suppresses it. _sanitize_func_name at src/haute/_graph_utils.py:105 does `name.replace(" ","_").replace("-","_")`, collapsing space and hyphen to the same identifier.
real.fix: In the mapped branch of _live_only_edges (src/haute/deploy/_pruner.py:58-69), do not `break` on first match. Collect ALL edges whose source label sanitizes to live_input_name; if more than one distinct source matches, raise a ValueError naming the colliding source labels/ids (mirroring the existing no-match ValueError and codegen's _error_on_name_collisions message), instead of silently keeping the first. Apply the same ambiguity check to the fallback inputs[0] branch (L51-57). A failing test should build two dataSource nodes with labels colliding only under sanitization (e.g. 'Live Source'/'Live-Source') feeding one liveSwitch and assert prune_for_deploy raises rather than returning an order-dependent parent.

real.title: Chart tab silently coerces/drops non-finite series values while Statistics tab throws into the ErrorBoundary
real.description: toQuoteRow reads each series value with Number(row[col] ?? 0). The ?? only catches null/undefined, so a genuinely-null cell becomes a fabricated 0 plotted on the chart, and a non-numeric value (e.g. the string 'n/a') becomes NaN. The Chart render path then propagates NaN into SVG geometry with no user-facing signal, whereas the Statistics tab feeds the exact same rows to computeScenarioStatsBySeries, whose readFiniteNumber THROWS on null/empty/non-finite. The result: identical preview data renders a silently-wrong/broken chart in the Chart tab but trips the panel's ErrorBoundary (App.tsx:647, replacing the whole preview with the error fallback) the instant the user switches to the Statistics tab. This is an inconsistent, silent-wrongness path that contradicts the project's 'fail loudly, no incorrect fallbacks' guidance.
real.evidence: Identical preview rows diverge. CHART (toQuoteRow line 50 `Number(row[col] ?? 0)`): null cell -> values [10,0,30] (fabricated 0); 'n/a' -> NaN flowing into SeriesLine path (line 265), producing SVG d="M44.0,189.6 L54.0,NaN L64.0,22.4" plus circle cx/cy=NaN (lines 275) with no signal; buildSeriesScale line 94 `v ?? 0` does NOT catch NaN (NaN ?? 0 === NaN). STATISTICS (computeScenarioStatsBySeries line 530 fed the SAME previewRows at line 531) -> readFiniteNumber line 34-35 THROWS `Expected finite numeric value in "loss", received null` / `received n/a`. The useMemo runs during render (line 528), so when tab==='statistics' the throw hits <ErrorBoundary name="DataPreview"> (App.tsx:584; getDerivedStateFromError renders the "Something went wrong" fallback). PreviewData.preview is Record<string,unknown>[] (DataPreview.tsx:18), so null/string cells are genuinely reachable (DataPreview even has NULL_VALUE_STYLE for them). Verified by executing the extracted logic in Node: all assertions on the specific wrong values passed.
real.fix: Make the Chart path validate value cells with the same strictness as Statistics. Route toQuoteRow's per-series and scenario-index/value coercions through optimiserScenarioStats.readFiniteNumber (export it), so a non-finite/null/non-numeric preview cell fails loudly in BOTH tabs (consistent with project "fail loudly, no incorrect fallbacks" guidance) instead of the chart silently fabricating 0 or emitting NaN into SVG geometry. Add a vitest covering both Scenario A (null cell) and Scenario B ('n/a' string): assert the chart no longer plots a fabricated value / no NaN reaches the SVG, and that both tabs surface the same error. Note for the implementer: the finding's evidence cites `ErrorBoundary name="NodePreview"` at App.tsx:647 - the actual catching boundary is `name="DataPreview"` opened at App.tsx:584 (647 is its closing tag); the catch mechanism is unaffected.
real.repro_path: n/a (frontend TS bug; proven by code-trace plus a self-contained Node execution of the extracted toQuoteRow/buildSeriesScale/SeriesLine vs readFiniteNumber logic, run from /tmp and removed). repro_outcome: divergence reproduced - chart yields [10,0,30] / SVG path containing literal 'NaN'; statistics throws on the identical rows.

real.title: failExploreJob relabels a previous explore report from a DIFFERENT config with the failed job's configHash, causing the panel to show stale cross-config data as the current result
real.description: On an explore failure, failExploreJob unconditionally preserves the previously cached report (`result: previous?.result ?? null`) but stamps the new entry with the FAILED job's identity (`configHash: job.configHash`, `source: job.source`, `structuralVersion: job.structuralVersion`). When the failure is for a config that differs from the previously successful one, the stored entry now claims an old report belongs to the new config. ExplorePreview's freshness check matches purely on configHash+source (currentCachedResult = cachedResult.configHash === configHash && cachedResult.source === activeSource), so it will surface the stale report (`report = currentCachedResult?.result`) as the result for the new config, with no staleness indicator (explore has no isStale gate, unlike solve/train via useStaleConfigEstimate). The fix is to preserve previous.result only when previous.configHash === job.configHash && previous.source === job.source, else null — matching the solve/train semantics where a failed run for a changed config does not present an old result as current.
real.evidence: failExploreJob (useNodeResultsStore.ts:1063-1071) builds nextCached = { result: previous?.result ?? null  // line 1064: keeps the LAST cached report; configHash: job.configHash  // line 1067: stamps the FAILED job's hash; source: job.source  // line 1068; error }. There is NO check that previous.configHash === job.configHash. The entry is keyed only by nodeId and is never evicted on config change (grep: exploreResults[nodeId] is only mutated by complete/failExploreJob; line 1062 reads it back; no clear-on-config-change path). ExplorePreview.tsx:91-95: currentCachedResult = cachedResult && cachedResult.configHash === configHash && cachedResult.source === activeSource ? cachedResult : null; report = currentCachedResult?.result ?? null — matches purely on configHash+source. ExplorePreview.tsx:96 sets status from terminalStatus but NO branch suppresses report when status is an error; report flows unconditionally to <ExploreOverviewPane report={report}/> (line 254). ExploreOverviewPane.tsx:81/95-104 renders report into DatasetSnapshotCard/SchemaTableCard/NumericSummaryCard etc. when report !== null; DatasetSnapshotCard shows report.row_count (ExploreSummaryCards.tsx:79) and report.columns (schema/null %). Trace: succeed config A -> exploreResults[n]={result:reportA,configHash:A}; change config to B (report correctly becomes null since A!==B); run explore for B (startExploreJob configHash=B) -> it fails -> failExploreJob: previous=A entry, nextCached={result:reportA,configHash:B,error}; now ExplorePreview matches (B===B) and renders reportA's row_count/schema/summaries as config B's data. NO staleness gate exists for explore: grep for isStale/stale in ExplorePreview.tsx returns nothing, whereas OptimiserConfig.tsx:1050-1053 shows a 'Config changed since last solve' banner via useStaleConfigEstimate (isStale = cachedResult.configHash !== configHash, hook line 60). The existing test useNodeResultsStore.test.ts:461-480 runs exactly this h1-succeed -> startExploreJob h2 -> failExploreJob sequence and asserts cached.result === report (line 478) without ever asserting configHash, codifying the mislabel as intended.
real.fix: In failExploreJob (useNodeResultsStore.ts:1062-1071), only carry the prior report forward when it belongs to the same config/source as the failed job: const previous = s.exploreResults[nodeId]; const keepPrevious = previous && previous.configHash === job.configHash && previous.source === job.source; then set result: keepPrevious ? previous.result : null. This preserves the legitimate 'a re-run of the SAME config failed, keep showing the last good report' behaviour while preventing a report from a DIFFERENT config from being relabeled as the failed job's. Also update the misleading test at useNodeResultsStore.test.ts:461-480: for the cross-config case (h1 -> h2) assert cached.configHash === 'h2' AND cached.result === null; add a same-config case (h1 succeed -> startExploreJob h1 -> failExploreJob) asserting cached.result === report to lock in the preserve-on-same-config path. Note: the finder's justification that this 'matches solve/train store semantics' is slightly imprecise — failSolveJob (lines 753-772) actually uses the same preserve-and-restamp pattern; the real solve/train safeguard is the UI-level useStaleConfigEstimate banner, which explore lacks. The proposed store-level fix is nonetheless the correct, minimal closure of the mislabeling.

real.title: Cache button enabled for emit-true tables with zero selected columns — build 'succeeds' but preview can never load
real.description: The cache-disable gate keys only on `t.emit` (`hasEmitTrue = v2.tables.some((t) => t.emit)`), but the backend's single source of truth for 'this table contributes a data port' is `table_is_emitting` = `emit AND at least one selected column` (`src/haute/_json_shred.py:155-176`). The frontend already mirrors this exact predicate in `apiInputPorts.ts` (`emitTables`/`hasSelectedColumn`, which the docstrings call the canonical mirror), but the editor does NOT use it here — it re-derives a weaker gate. Consequence: a schema with an emit-true table but no selected columns (e.g. immediately after clicking 'Add Table', which creates `emit:true, columns:[]`, or after the user unticks every column) enables the cache button. `build_per_port_cache` then computes `emit_tables = []`, writes a meta.json with empty tables, and the build returns success (the button flips to 'Refresh Cache'). But `load_v2_api_source` raises RuntimeError on the very next preview/run: 'API Input has emit-true tables but none has any selected columns…' (`_json_shred.py:1006-1013`). The `disabledReason` text is also wrong — 'Toggle at least one table's emit so it produces a port' — emit alone does NOT produce a port.
real.evidence: Frontend code-trace: ApiInputEditor.tsx:397 `const hasEmitTrue = v2.tables.some((t) => t.emit)` -> :398 `cacheDisabled = !hasSchemaSource || !hasEmitTrue`; reason :402 "Toggle at least one table's emit so it produces a port." The canonical mirror apiInputPorts.ts:50-66 `emitTables` additionally requires `hasSelectedColumn` (its docstring lines 56-63 say an emit-true zero-selected table is NOT emitted at runtime), and the editor never imports it (only apiInputLabelIssue/Message). Reachable states: addTable (ApiInputEditor.tsx:259-276) creates `emit: v2.tables.length===0, columns: []` -> first table is emit:true with zero columns; column checkbox at :692-693 lets a user untick every column while emit stays true. Backend executed-repro output line: build summary `tables == []` (table_count=0), `is_per_port_cache_valid == True`, then `load_v2_api_source` raised: "API Input has emit-true tables but none has any selected columns. ... tick at least one column on the emitting table(s): ['root']." build_per_port_cache (_json_shred.py:776) only calls validate_v2_schema, which per its documented invariants (_api_input_schema.py:266-291) does NOT require any emitting table; the build filters emit_tables via table_is_emitting (_json_shred.py:811-821) to [] and returns success (:895-902); validity loop (_json_shred.py:1068-1073) skips non-emitting tables so the empty cache is "valid"; load rejects at _json_shred.py:1006-1013. No guard elsewhere prevents the enabled button.
real.fix: Make the editor gate reuse the canonical port predicate instead of re-deriving a weaker one. In ApiInputEditor.tsx (lines 396-403), replace `hasEmitTrue = v2.tables.some((t) => t.emit)` with the existing mirror — e.g. export a small `hasEmitPort(config)` from utils/apiInputPorts.ts (true iff `emitTables(config).length > 0`, i.e. some table is emit:true AND has >=1 selected column) and gate on that. Also fix `disabledReason` to reflect the real requirement, e.g. "Tick at least one column on an emit-true table so it produces a port." Add a frontend test (ApiInputEditor.test.tsx) asserting the cache button is disabled with the corrected tooltip for a single table `{emit:true, columns:[]}` and for an emit-true table whose every column is unticked, and enabled once a column is selected. This keeps the gate, the rendered handles, and the backend load predicate in lockstep.

real.title: Export-tab "Result detail" is point-specific but only reset on jobId change, so it goes stale (and keeps Save/Log disabled) after selecting a different frontier point
real.description: handleLoadResultDetail issues applyOptimiser with `point_index: selectedIdx` (L327), making the loaded ApplyOptimiserResponse specific to the currently selected frontier point. ResultDetailStatus then renders that point's row counts ("{returnedRows} of {totalRows} rows loaded", L810-822). But resultDetail is reset to idle ONLY when jobId changes (effect at L185-188 with deps [abortResultDetailRequest, jobId]); there is no reset when selectedIdx changes. So: load detail for point A (status becomes 'loaded'), then click point B (same job, so no reset) -> the Export tab still shows point A's row counts, attributed to the now-selected point B. Compounding this, terminalDetailBlocksActions = resultDetail.status === 'loading' || 'loaded' (L169) is passed as terminalActionsDisabled to both ExportTab (L465) and the Frontier DetailCard (L427); since 'loaded' is a persistent state never cleared on selection change, the Save Result and Log to MLflow buttons stay disabled across point selections (and effectively until the next jobId / 'Refresh detail') even though the user is now looking at a different, un-previewed point.
real.evidence: OptimiserPreview.tsx L327 sends `point_index: selectedIdx` to applyOptimiser (per-point response). The ONLY reset effect is L185-188 `useEffect(() => { abortResultDetailRequest(); setResultDetail({status:'idle'}) }, [abortResultDetailRequest, jobId])`; `abortResultDetailRequest` is a stable `useCallback(...,[])` (L181-184), so the effect re-runs ONLY when `jobId` changes. useNodeResultsStore.ts `selectFrontierPoint` (L792-812) spreads `...cached` and changes only `selectedPointIndex` + `result`, leaving `jobId` identical, so clicking a new point updates `displayData.selectedPointIndex` (=> `selectedIdx`) without touching `jobId`. Therefore `resultDetail` is NOT reset on selection change: ResultDetailStatus (L810-817) keeps showing point A's `row_count`/`preview_row_count` (test L996: "100 of 1,250 rows loaded") while point B is selected, and `terminalDetailBlocksActions = status==='loading'||'loaded'` (L169) stays true, keeping Save/Log disabled in both ExportTab (L687,719,741) and DetailCard (L113,185,199). Existing tests corroborate: the per-point apply test (L1018-1035) confirms detail is point-specific, and the only reset test (L1037-1059) is keyed on jobId change ("aborts ... when the job changes", rerender with jobId:"job_456") — no test exercises a selection change after load.
real.fix: Add `selectedIdx` to the reset effect's dependency array (L185-188) so loaded/in-flight result detail is aborted and cleared to idle whenever the selected frontier point changes (mirroring the existing jobId reset). Concretely: `useEffect(() => { abortResultDetailRequest(); setResultDetail({ status: "idle" }) }, [abortResultDetailRequest, jobId, selectedIdx])`. This makes the per-point ApplyOptimiserResponse no longer outlive its point: ResultDetailStatus row counts can never be attributed to a different point, and terminalDetailBlocksActions returns to false on selection so Save Result / Log to MLflow re-enable for the newly selected point until the user clicks "Load detail" again. Add a regression test in OptimiserPreview.test.tsx (Export tab block) that: loads detail for point 0 (asserts "rows loaded" + Save disabled), then rerenders/clicks to select point 1 with the same jobId, and asserts the ResultDetailStatus is gone and Save result is re-enabled.

real.title: Downstream preview cascade mixes submodel edges with parent-graph nodes, so the cascade is silently dead when a node inside an opened submodel changes columns
real.description: Inside fetchPreviewImmediate the cascade builds its adjacency from graphRef.current.edges but resolves its node set from resolveGraphFromRefs(...).nodes. When a submodel is drilled in, graphRef.current holds the SUBMODEL canvas (nodes+edges) while parentGraphRef.current is set, so resolveGraphFromRefs returns the PARENT graph's nodes. propagate therefore walks submodel edge IDs to compute reachableNodeIds, but drainReadyQueue looks those submodel child IDs up in cascadeNodes (= parent nodes) via cascadeNodes.find(n => n.id === nodeId). The lookup misses every time, so each downstream child hits the `if (!dsNode || !canPreviewNode(dsNode)) { settleNode(nodeId, false); continue }` branch and the cascade no-ops: downstream nodes inside a submodel never get re-previewed (their _columns / requestedPreviewColumns are not refreshed) after an upstream column change. At the top level parentGraphRef.current is null so resolveGraphFromRefs returns graphRef.current.edges/nodes and the two sources coincide — the defect is submodel-specific.

real.title: handleCellClick has no request-sequence / abort guard — out-of-order trace responses desync tracedCell vs traceResult and can clobber a newer trace with a stale one
real.description: handleCellClick synchronously sets tracedCell = {rowIndex, column} for the just-clicked cell, then fires an async traceCell() request whose .then sets traceResult. There is no AbortSignal, no in-flight request tracking, and no "is this still the latest request" check. If a user clicks cell A then cell B before A resolves, both requests run concurrently; whichever resolves LAST wins setTraceResult. When A resolves after B, the node/edge decorations and trace panel (driven by traceResult) show A's trace while the highlighted cell (driven by tracedCell, App.tsx -> DataPreview line 365 isTraced) shows B — a user-visible inconsistency, and the freshly-requested B trace is silently overwritten by the stale A trace.

Consumers diverge: tracedCell -> DataPreview.tsx:365 `isTraced={tracedCell?.rowIndex===i && tracedCell?.column===col.name}`; traceResult -> nodesWithStatus(354), edgesWithTrace(426), trace panel. Only call site (grep: traceCell at useTracing.ts:211 only); App.tsx:598/642 wire handleCellClick straight to onCellClick with no debounce. Node simulation faithfully mirroring 210-228 asserts the wrong values: final tracedCell=B(row5,premium) but traceResult=stale trace-A(row0,price); fresh B clobbered. Either approach prevents an earlier click's response from overwriting a newer one. Add a useTracing test that interleaves two handleCellClick calls with deferred promises resolved in reverse order and asserts the final traceResult corresponds to the second (latest) click and matches tracedCell.

real.title: Ctrl+Shift+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z redo is unreachable (contradictory key+shift check) — breaks keyboard redo, the only redo shortcut on macOS
real.description: The redo branch requires `mod && e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey && !isTyping`. Therefore the condition `e.key === "z" && e.shiftKey` can never be simultaneously true: when `shiftKey` is true the key is `"Z"`. The standard redo accelerator Ctrl+Shift+Z (Windows/Linux) and Cmd+Shift+Z (macOS) is dead. On macOS there is no Ctrl+Y fallback (line 60 only helps Windows users), so keyboard redo is completely non-functional for Mac users. The undo branch at line 49 (`e.key === "z" && !e.shiftKey`) works because Ctrl alone does not alter the character.

Add a regression test that fires the realistic event `fireKey("Z", { metaKey: true, shiftKey: true })` (uppercase key, the value real browsers emit) and asserts redo is called; the artificial key:"z"+shift test should be corrected/removed since it cannot occur in a browser. real.title: All letter-key shortcuts silently break when CapsLock is on (no e.key case normalization)
real.description: Every letter shortcut compares the raw `e.key` against a lowercase literal: Ctrl+S (`"s"`), Ctrl+Z (`"z"`), Ctrl+Y (`"y"`), Ctrl+C (`"c"`), Ctrl+V (`"v"`), Ctrl+A (`"a"`), Ctrl+K (`"k"`), Ctrl+G (`"g"`). When CapsLock is active, the browser reports the uppercase key value (e.g. `e.key === "S"`), so none of these comparisons match and every letter shortcut — including save, undo, copy, paste, select-all — silently stops working with no feedback. The handler never normalizes case (no `e.key.toLowerCase()`), so the behaviour depends on the user's CapsLock state. MDN KeyboardEvent.key: the value is the case-adjusted printable character considering modifier state — with CapsLock ON a letter key yields `"S"`, so `"S" === "s"` is false and every letter branch is skipped. real.title: Stale-response race: out-of-order getRuns/getModelVersions can overwrite current data
real.description: refreshRuns and refreshVersions fire an un-cancellable fetch and unconditionally apply the result in .then. The fetch guard (fetchedRunsFor / fetchedVersionsFor) only prevents duplicate in-flight fetches for the SAME key; it does not discard a response for a stale key. When the user switches experiments, MlflowModelPicker (ExperimentRunPicker onChange, MlflowModelPicker.tsx:182-184) calls setRuns([]), resetRunsGuard(), then refreshRuns(newExpId). If the previous getRuns(oldExpId) is still in flight, its .then runs setRuns(oldData) whenever it resolves and can land AFTER the new experiment's data, leaving the dropdown showing runs from the wrong experiment. Same pattern for refreshVersions on a fast model switch. getRuns/getModelVersions already accept an AbortSignal (api/client.ts:1032,1047) but the hook never passes one nor tracks a request id, so there is no last-write-wins protection.
real.evidence: useMlflowBrowser.ts:112-121 refreshRuns: line 118 `getRuns(expId, runTag).then(data => { setRuns(...); setLoadingRuns(false) })` — no AbortSignal passed (despite client.ts:1029-1037 `getRuns(experimentId, artifactFilter?, options?: {signal?})` accepting one) and no request-id/sequence check in the `.then`. The only guard `fetchedRunsFor` (line 114-115) gates fetch START, not response APPLY. MlflowModelPicker.tsx:177-185 onChange runs `setBrowseExpId(eid); setRuns([]); resetRunsGuard(); if(eid) refreshRuns(eid)` — resetRunsGuard sets fetchedRunsFor.current="" (hook:147), so when switching old->new, two getRuns promises are in flight and the final `runs` state is whichever `.then` resolves LAST, not whichever was requested last. If getRuns(old) resolves after getRuns(new), `setRuns(oldData)` lands while browseExpId==="new" => dropdown shows runs from the wrong experiment. refreshVersions (hook:133-144) is identical (line 141 `getModelVersions(modelName)` no signal, line 142 unconditional setModelVersions). The component render-guard `modelVersionsFor === selectedModel` (MlflowModelPicker.tsx:35) does NOT save it because modelVersionsFor is set SYNCHRONOUSLY at call time (hook:138), so after switching to modelB it already equals "modelB"; a late modelA `.then` writes modelA's versions and the guard "modelB"==="modelB" passes, displaying stale data. Grep confirmed: zero AbortController/.signal/requestId/sequence/generation in the hook.
real.fix: Add per-call last-write-wins protection in useMlflowBrowser. Minimal: introduce a monotonically-increasing ref per resource (e.g. runsReqIdRef/versionsReqIdRef); capture `const myId = ++ref.current` before the fetch and in both `.then` and `.catch` apply state only if `myId === ref.current`. Better/idiomatic given the API already supports it: track an AbortController per resource in a ref, abort the previous controller at the start of each refreshRuns/refreshVersions, pass `{ signal: controller.signal }` into getRuns/getModelVersions, and ignore AbortError in `.catch`. Either approach discards stale responses so the dropdown always reflects the most recently requested experiment/model. Add regression tests that mock getRuns/getModelVersions to resolve out of order (old resolves after new) and assert `runs`/`modelVersions` reflect the LATEST requested key.

real.title: Modal focus effect re-runs on every parent re-render (unstable onClose/extraCloseKeys deps), yanking focus out of the modal and corrupting focus restoration
real.description: The mount/focus effect depends on [onClose, extraCloseKeys]. Each re-render gives ModalShell new dep references, so the effect's cleanup+setup fire every time: the cleanup runs `previousFocusRef.current.focus()` (pulls focus back to the pre-modal background element), then the setup overwrites `previousFocusRef.current = document.activeElement` and calls `containerRef.current?.focus()` (yanks focus to the modal container). Net effect: while the user hovers nodes in the background graph, the open modal repeatedly steals focus back to its container, so the user cannot keep keyboard focus on an inner control (e.g. Tab-navigating the shortcuts list or typing in RenameDialog's textarea is interrupted), and the saved restore target is repeatedly reset.

real.title: include_main all-or-nothing guard still causes duplicate-main-effect singularity on partial factor overlap
real.description: The guard sets include_main=False only when ALL interaction factors are already in the main `terms` dict, and otherwise forwards include_main (default True). But RustyStats' include_main=True adds main effects for EVERY factor in the interaction. When an interaction mixes factors that ARE already standalone main terms with factors that are NOT (a partial overlap), include_main=True re-adds the main effect for the already-present factor, producing exactly the duplicated main effect / perfect-collinearity / singular-matrix error the docstring (lines 69-74, 89-90) claims to prevent. The guard's premise ('set include_main=True when at least one factor is NOT in terms') is incomplete: a single missing factor flips the whole interaction to include_main=True even though the other, present, factors must NOT get their main effects re-added. RustyStats exposes include_main only as one boolean for the whole interaction, so the present design cannot add only the missing main effects — the partial-overlap case is structurally mishandled.
real.evidence: Repro output: partial main_effects = ['age', 'age', 'region']; design columns = ['Intercept', 'age', 'age', 'region[T.B]', 'region[T.C]', 'region[T.B]:age', 'region[T.C]:age'] (two identical 'age' columns at idx [1,2]); partial-overlap fit raised ValueError: "GLM fitting failed: Linear algebra error: Failed to solve linear system - matrix may be singular. This often indicates multicollinearity in predictors." while the all-overlap control fit succeeded. Code-trace corroboration: RustyStats formula.py:2597-2609 re-parses every factor (no dedup) on include_main=True, formula.py:2208 appends 'age' to main_effects a second time, and interactions.py:1277-1308 emits one design column per main_effects entry with no deduplication.
real.fix: Replace the all-or-nothing include_main boolean with per-factor handling so only the MISSING factors get their main effects in. In _build_interactions, always set rs_int["include_main"]=False (RustyStats must not re-add any present factor's main effect), and for each interaction factor that is NOT already in `terms`, add it to the main `terms` dict as a standalone term (e.g. terms.setdefault(factor, {"type": "categorical"}) or the factor's own spec) before building the design. That way every factor has exactly one main effect and the interaction product is added without duplication, eliminating the singular-matrix path for the partial-overlap case. Add a fit-level regression test (not just an assertion on the dict) using a partial-overlap interaction to lock the behaviour.

real.title: Temporal mask ignores holdout_size when validation_size==0: holdout swallows ALL post-cutoff rows
real.description: In _temporal_mask the post-cutoff data is split between validation and holdout using holdout_frac = holdout_size / (validation_size + holdout_size). When validation_size == 0 (a valid, explicit request meaning 'no validation set'), this fraction collapses to holdout_size/holdout_size = 1.0, so EVERY post-cutoff row is assigned to holdout regardless of the requested holdout_size. The requested holdout fraction is silently discarded. The subsequent reclassification block (lines 316-318, 'if validation_size == 0: VALIDATION -> TRAIN') cannot help because there are no VALIDATION rows left to convert. This contradicts the documented semantics of holdout_size (a fraction of the dataset, honoured exactly by the sibling _random_mask) and produces a holdout set far larger than requested with no error or warning. The realised holdout fraction equals the entire post-cutoff portion of the data, which is driven by cutoff_date, not by holdout_size at all.
real.evidence: Executed repro output: "TEMPORAL (val=0.0, holdout=0.1): {0: 14, 1: 0, 2: 6}" vs "RANDOM (val=0.0, holdout=0.1): {0: 18, 1: 0, 2: 2}". All assertions passed (exit 0), confirming temporal holdout = ALL 6 post-cutoff rows (30% of dataset) while random honours holdout_size=0.1 -> 2 rows. Decisive follow-up: with validation_size=0, sweeping holdout_size in {0.05,0.1,0.3,0.5,0.9,0.99} ALL yield HOLDOUT=6 — the magnitude of the user-set holdout_size knob is completely inert. The discontinuity is a degenerate cliff, not a smooth limit: validation_size 0.0->6, 0.01->5, 0.05->4, 0.1->3. Root cause confirmed at _split.py:302 holdout_frac = holdout_size/(validation_size+holdout_size) = 0.1/0.1 = 1.0, then line 312 n_holdout = int(6*1.0) = 6. Input is reachable/unguarded: __post_init__ (lines 28-43) permits validation_size=0 with holdout_size>0, and _training_job.py:361 does SplitConfig(**split) straight from user config (routes/modelling.py:360).
real.fix: In _temporal_mask, stop deriving n_holdout from the validation/holdout ratio. Honour holdout_size as a fraction of the whole dataset, matching the sibling _random_mask/_group_mask: n_holdout = min(int(n_total * holdout_size), n_non_train), assigned to the most-recent rows of the post-cutoff slice; then n_validation = min(int(n_total * validation_size), n_non_train - n_holdout) takes the next-most-recent slice. This removes the degenerate validation_size==0 cliff (where holdout_frac collapses to 1.0 and the requested fraction is discarded) and makes holdout_size's magnitude meaningful for every validation_size, including 0. Add a regression test: strategy=temporal, validation_size=0.0, holdout_size=0.1 on a frame with many post-cutoff rows must yield a holdout of ~int(n_total*0.1), not the entire post-cutoff region; plus a test asserting holdout_size=0.1 vs 0.5 give different holdout counts when validation_size==0.

real.title: Group mask validation fallback is a no-op when no TRAIN group exists, leaving both validation AND train empty
real.description: The 'ensure at least one validation group' fallback (lines 352-358) only fires when no group landed in VALIDATION, and it tries to flip the first group that is currently labelled PARTITION_TRAIN into VALIDATION. But when holdout_size is large relative to the (few) groups, it is possible for EVERY unique group to hash below holdout_size and be assigned PARTITION_HOLDOUT — so there is no TRAIN group for the loop to convert. The loop iterates, finds no group with value PARTITION_TRAIN, and breaks out having changed nothing. The result is that validation_size > 0 was requested but the validation partition is silently empty, AND the train partition is also empty (every row is holdout). Training then proceeds on zero rows with no error. The known catalog finding #51 explicitly assumes 'the only correction triggers solely on no_validation' and that it succeeds when it fires; this is the distinct failure mode where the correction fires but is ineffective because its precondition (an available TRAIN group) is not guaranteed.
real.evidence: Ran `uv run python review/04-exhaustive/repro/V095.py` (polars present). Output: "mask (internal _group_mask) = [2, 2, 2, 2, 2]"; "internal counts: train=0 validation=0 holdout=5"; "requested: validation_size=0.2 (>0) holdout_size=0.6"; then "AssertionError: EXPECTED at least one TRAIN row ... but got n_train=0 (all rows holdout)" with EXIT_CODE=1. Both the internal _group_mask and the public split_mask produce the identical mask. Independent hash check: md5 frac(seed=2,'A')=0.024889 and frac('B')=0.036948, both < holdout_size=0.6, so both groups hit PARTITION_HOLDOUT at _split.py:344-345 — no group is PARTITION_TRAIN, so the fallback loop at _split.py:355-358 finds nothing to convert and is a no-op (it only flips a group whose label == PARTITION_TRAIN, line 356). The failure is a demonstrably wrong VALUE (empty train AND empty validation despite validation_size=0.2 requested), not an import/setup error.
real.fix: In _group_mask, after building group_partition, enforce the requested partitions instead of only patching the no_validation case. (1) Guarantee >=1 TRAIN group when train_frac>0 (validation_size+holdout_size<1): if no group is PARTITION_TRAIN, reclassify one group (e.g. the highest-hash / lowest-priority HOLDOUT group) to TRAIN. (2) For the validation fallback at lines 352-358, when validation_size>0 and no group is VALIDATION, convert a group regardless of current label (prefer a TRAIN group, else fall back to a HOLDOUT group) so validation is never silently empty. With few groups, an exact-count assignment (sort groups by hash, allocate the minimum counts each partition needs) is more robust than independent per-group Bernoulli draws. Additionally/alternatively, per CLAUDE.md fail-loud policy, add a guard in _training_job._split_data that raises ValueError when n_train==0 (and when validation was requested but n_validation==0), naming requested vs realised partition sizes. Note: distinct from catalog finding #51, which covers fraction over/under-shoot and explicitly assumes the no_validation correction succeeds when it fires; V095 is the case where it fires but is ineffective because holdout_size>0 routes every group to HOLDOUT (line 344) leaving no TRAIN group.

real.title: Online frontier-point /apply full-clears quote_grid/solver, ending the frontier session and breaking a subsequent apply of a different point
real.description: In apply_lambdas, the frontier-point branch (target_point_index is not None) calls _store.clear_result_data(body.job_id) with no keys argument, which defaults to the full _HEAVY_OBJECT_KEYS set = ('solver','solve_result','quote_grid','factors_df','ratebook_factor_contexts'). This wipes quote_grid and solver even though the user is mid frontier-analysis (they just applied a specific frontier point). Every OTHER frontier-session exit in this module deliberately preserves that heavy state: the non-frontier apply branch (line 1330) and the save/mlflow paths use _clear_result_data_after_user_action, which keeps quote_grid/solver when the job still has frontier points and only strips solve_result; and the ratebook frontier-select/apply paths (lines 1485, 1507) clear only ('solve_result',). The helper _clear_result_data_after_user_action exists precisely for this: its docstring says 'Slim result data without ending an active frontier-analysis session' (line 664), and _job_has_frontier_points gates retention. Consequence: after applying online frontier point 0, applying a DIFFERENT point N (which has no cached frontier_apply_result:N artifact) re-enters _materialise_frontier_point_apply and hits _store.touch_heavy_objects(job_id, required_keys=('quote_grid',)) at line 1025, which now returns False because quote_grid was cleared, raising HTTP 400 'Quote grid is not available for this job. Re-run the solve to materialise this frontier point.' (lines 1026-1042). The online apply path even persists per-point artifacts and carries its own re-run-the-solve copy, signalling an intended multi-point session, yet it self-destructs the runtime state needed for it after the first apply.
real.evidence: Executed repro (exit 0, all asserts pass): "first apply status: 200" -> "after first apply: frontier points still present = True" + "after first apply: quote_grid present = False" -> "second apply status: 400" with body {"detail":"Quote grid is not available for this job. Re-run the solve to materialise this frontier point."}. The first online frontier-point apply (point 0) returns 200 and full-clears quote_grid even though the job still holds 2 frontier points (session active); a subsequent apply of a DIFFERENT valid point (point 1) then 400s. Correct behaviour would be 200 (materialise point 1 against the still-live quote_grid), matching the symmetric exits.
real.fix: In apply_lambdas, replace the frontier-point branch's `_store.clear_result_data(body.job_id)` at optimiser.py:1288 with `_clear_result_data_after_user_action(body.job_id)` — the exact helper already used by the non-frontier apply branch (line 1330), save_result (1636), and mlflow_log. That helper preserves heavy runtime state (solver/quote_grid) while `_job_has_frontier_points(job)` is True and strips only solve_result, keeping the frontier-analysis session alive so other points can still be materialised; it falls back to the full clear when no frontier points remain. Add a regression test mirroring the ratebook symmetry test (tests/test_optimiser_routes.py:9780-9858) for the ONLINE path: inject a 2-point online frontier job, apply point 0 (200), assert job still has 'solver' and 'quote_grid', then apply point 1 and assert 200 (not 400).

real.title: Save-time apiInput cache mirror resolves data path only against project_root, diverging from the cache-build resolution for nested pipelines — committed/ is silently never promoted
real.description: `_mirror_api_input_caches` resolves each apiInput data file as `data_path = (self._root / path).resolve()` (project_root only). It then calls `mirror_cache_to_committed(str(data_path))`, whose first gate is `_is_working_consulted(data_path)` — a check keyed by `_path_hash` = SHA-256 of the canonical resolved path. The cache *build* path (`routes/json_cache.py::_resolve_data_path`) resolves the SAME logical apiInput path via `resolve_runtime_file_path(path, pipeline_dir=pipeline_dir(), project_root=Path.cwd(), prefer='project', enforce_project_root=True)`, which falls back to the *pipeline-relative* location when the project-root candidate does not exist, and marks THAT resolved path consulted via `_mark_working_consulted`. For a nested pipeline (`pipeline_root != project_root`, a first-class supported config — see `__init__` validating `pipeline_root.is_relative_to(project_root)`, and `pipeline_dir()` returning the configured `[project].pipeline` parent) whose apiInput references a data file relatively (e.g. `path='data/quotes.json'`) that physically lives under the pipeline directory (`<pipeline_root>/data/quotes.json`) and NOT under the project root, the two resolutions diverge: build resolves to `<pipeline_root>/data/quotes.json`; mirror resolves to `<root>/data/quotes.json`. Different paths -> different `_path_hash` -> `_is_working_consulted` returns False for the mirror's hash -> `mirror_cache_to_committed` short-circuits to a no-op (returns False). Result: the working cache the editor built is never promoted to committed/, so the committed/deployed pipeline serves a stale or missing cache while the editor shows the fresh one. The failure is silent (no warning — the mirror simply no-ops the consulted-gate).
real.evidence: Repro (exit 0) output: build-resolved data_path = <tmp>/nested/data/quotes.json (hash 3692ab32...), mirror-resolved data_path = <tmp>/data/quotes.json (hash d66c48c7...); consulted(build_resolved)=True, consulted(mirror_resolved)=False; working/(build hash) exists=True but committed/(build hash) exists after save=False — the save mirror was a silent no-op. CONTROL: mirror_cache_to_committed(build_resolved) returned True and created committed/, proving working/ was promotable and the no-op was caused solely by the project-root-only path resolution. Corroborated by code-trace: pipeline.py:373 builds SavePipelineService(project_root=Path.cwd(), pipeline_root=pipeline_dir()); _save_pipeline.py:623 mirror uses data_path=(self._root/path).resolve() (project-root only) while json_cache.py:146-159 build and execution.py:178-184 runtime both use resolve_runtime_file_path(..., pipeline_dir=..., prefer='project') which falls back to the pipeline-relative file (_path_resolution.py:101-128); _json_flatten.py:111-113/258-260 gate the mirror on _path_hash equality, so the divergent path makes mirror_cache_to_committed return False.
real.fix: In SavePipelineService._mirror_api_input_caches (src/haute/routes/_save_pipeline.py:616-633), resolve the apiInput data path the same way the build route and the executor do, instead of (self._root / path).resolve(). Replace the resolution with resolve_runtime_file_path(path, pipeline_dir=self._pipeline_root, project_root=self._root, prefer="project", enforce_project_root=True) (matching json_cache._resolve_data_path / execution.py's prefer="project" fallback), then pass that resolved path to mirror_cache_to_committed. This makes the mirror's _path_hash identical to the build/runtime cache key so committed/ is promoted for nested pipelines. enforce_project_root keeps the traversal guard (the explicit is_relative_to check becomes redundant). Add a regression test mirroring tests/test_json_cache_integrity.py::test_http_build_save_restart_serves_from_committed but with source_file under a nested pipeline dir (pipeline_root != project_root) and a data file that exists only at the pipeline-relative location, asserting committed/ exists after save and load_v2_api_source serves from it after a simulated restart.

real.title: train_status raises TypeError (500) when a job's timeout is non-numeric (e.g. JSON null) from user config
real.description: train_status reads `timeout = job.get("timeout", _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)` and then evaluates `if start and (time.monotonic() - start) > timeout:`. The `timeout` value stored on the job is taken verbatim from the modelling node's free-form config: in _launch_background, `_store.atomic_update(job_id, {..., "timeout": config.get("timeout", _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)})`. `node.data.config` is typed `dict[str, Any]` (src/haute/_types.py:599) with no validation/coercion of `timeout` anywhere (confirmed: no `timeout` handling in _train_config.py or schemas.py). If a user sets `"timeout": null` (a realistic value when clearing the field) the key is present with value None, so `dict.get(key, default)` returns None — NOT _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT — and the comparison `(time.monotonic() - start) > None` raises `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'NoneType'`. A string value (e.g. `"3600"`) fails the same way. Because _launch_background sets `start_time` together with `timeout` for every started job, the comparison branch is taken on every poll once the job is running, so each /train/status/{job_id} request returns a 500 and the user can never observe the running job's progress or terminal state. This is strictly worse than failing loudly at config time because the job keeps running while its status endpoint is permanently broken.
real.evidence: Repro output: Case A (stored timeout=None, i.e. config `timeout: null`) -> `train_status -> TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'NoneType'`; Case B (timeout="3600") -> `TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'float' and 'str'`; Control (timeout=3600 int) -> `OK, status='running'`. Mechanism check printed `{"timeout": null}.get("timeout", _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) -> None` (NOT 3600). modelling.py:67-68 compares the raw stored value with no isinstance guard; _train_service.py:1052 stores `config.get("timeout", _DEFAULT_TIMEOUT)` verbatim; _validate_config (lines 643-668), _train_config.py, and schemas.py never touch `timeout`; _types.py:599 `config: dict[str, Any]` is unvalidated. The sibling optimiser path guards correctly (optimiser.py:1207-1213 `isinstance(timeout, int | float)` + _optimiser_service.py:425-428 `_solve_timeout_from_config`/`_optional_positive_int`), which is exactly the guard the modelling path is missing — confirming this is a genuine inconsistency, not a mitigated edge case.
real.fix: Mirror the optimiser's defensive pattern. Add a `_train_timeout_from_config(config)` helper (analogous to `_solve_timeout_from_config` in _optimiser_service.py) that routes through a positive-int coercion: treat missing key as `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT`, treat `None`/"" as `_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (since modelling always wants a finite ceiling), and raise a 400/TrainingConfigError on genuinely invalid types/values. Use it at _train_service.py:1052 so the stored `timeout` is always an int. Defensively, also add the optimiser-style `isinstance(timeout, int | float) and not isinstance(timeout, bool) and timeout > 0` guard at modelling.py:68 so a malformed stored value can never 500 the status poll. Add a regression test that creates a running job with `timeout=None` (and `timeout="3600"`) and asserts `/train/status/{job_id}` returns 200 rather than raising TypeError, plus a config-validation test asserting a non-numeric `timeout` is rejected at start() time.

real.title: _is_stale ignores Vite's root index.html and public/ assets, so edits there ship stale and skip rebuild
real.description: _is_stale only treats files under frontend/src/ (rglob of *.ts/*.tsx/*.css/*.html) plus a fixed config list (vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, tsconfig.app.json, package.json) as build inputs. But the Vite build (frontend/vite.config.ts: outDir '../src/haute/static', emptyOutDir true) has two additional first-class inputs that are NOT scanned: (1) frontend/index.html — the actual Vite entry HTML at the frontend ROOT (it references /favicon.svg and /src/main.tsx and is transformed into static/index.html), and (2) everything under frontend/public/ (favicon.svg, vite.svg) which Vite copies verbatim into the output. Because src_dir.rglob('*.html') is rooted at frontend/src, the root frontend/index.html never matches, and frontend/public/ is never walked. Consequence, in two places: in initialize() line 50, when HAUTE_BUILD_FRONTEND=1 the rebuild is skipped (returns early) even though the entry HTML or a public asset changed; and in _validate_static_assets() line 85 a normal wheel build passes validation even though the packaged static/ is genuinely older than the changed input. This is exactly the failure the module exists to prevent (module docstring lines 1-6; _validate_static_assets docstring line 77: 'Fail clearly when a wheel build would package missing or stale frontend'). A developer who edits the page <title>, meta tags, favicon, or the script entry in frontend/index.html, then builds a wheel, silently ships the previous build's index.html. Secondary instance of the same gap: tsconfig.node.json (which exists in frontend/) is also absent from the config list, though its build impact is weaker than index.html/public.
real.evidence: Repro output: "control (src/App.tsx edited) -> is_stale = True" / "BUG1 (frontend/index.html edited) -> is_stale = False" / "BUG2 (public/favicon.svg edited) -> is_stale = False". Editing the real Vite entry frontend/index.html (which references /src/main.tsx and /favicon.svg, title 'haute', transformed by Vite into static/index.html) or frontend/public/favicon.svg AFTER the build leaves the packaged static/index.html genuinely stale, yet _is_stale (hatch_build.py:93-107) returns False because it only rglobs frontend/src for *.ts/*.tsx/*.css/*.html plus the fixed config list ['vite.config.ts','tsconfig.json','tsconfig.app.json','package.json']. The control (changed src/App.tsx detected as True) confirms the harness is sound and the gap is specific. Verified on disk: frontend/index.html (419B), frontend/public/{favicon.svg,vite.svg}, and frontend/tsconfig.node.json all exist; no .html exists under frontend/src; no other guard scans these paths.
real.fix: In hatch_build.py:_is_stale, treat the root frontend/index.html and everything under frontend/public/ as build inputs, and add tsconfig.node.json to the config list. Minimal patch: after the src rglob loop, add `if (frontend_dir / "index.html").exists() and (frontend_dir / "index.html").stat().st_mtime > build_mtime: return True`, walk `for f in (frontend_dir / "public").rglob("*"): if f.is_file() and f.stat().st_mtime > build_mtime: return True`, and add "tsconfig.node.json" to the config tuple. Preferred (less brittle than a hand-maintained allowlist): rglob the whole frontend_dir and compare any file's mtime to build_mtime while pruning node_modules/, dist/, and the output static dir. Add regression tests asserting _is_stale returns True when only frontend/index.html or a frontend/public/ asset is newer than static/index.html (extend tests/test_hatch_build.py, which currently covers only the missing-assets path).

real.title: get_status.changed_files mangles renamed files into a single 'old -> new' string
real.description: When a file has been renamed, `git status --porcelain` emits a single line of the form `R  old.py -> new.py` (status code 'R', two-char status + space, then 'old -> new'). The parser does `line[3:].strip().strip('"')`, which yields the literal string `old.py -> new.py` as ONE entry in `changed_files`, instead of the new path `new.py`. Consequently the status panel shows a nonsensical pseudo-filename for every rename, and any consumer treating entries as real paths (e.g. opening the file) breaks. The same line[3:] slice also fails to C-unescape git's quoted paths (git emits `"my file.py"` / backslash-escaped octal for non-ASCII and special chars); `.strip('"')` removes only the outer quotes and leaves embedded escapes intact. Note save_progress/_auto_commit are unaffected because they parse `git diff --cached --name-only`, which prints each path on its own line with no arrow form — only get_status uses the porcelain arrow format.
real.evidence: Repro output: changed_files = ['a.py -> b.py', 'na\\303\\257ve.py']. Raw porcelain parsed was `R  a.py -> b.py` and `A  "na\303\257ve.py"`. Expected entries are ['b.py', 'naïve.py']. Both produced entries report exists_on_disk=False, proving they are not usable paths. The slice at src/haute/_git.py:388 `changed_files.append(line[3:].strip().strip('"'))` keeps the arrow form verbatim (rename mangled) and leaves git's octal C-escapes intact (.strip('"') only removes outer quotes).
real.fix: Parse `git status --porcelain` robustly in get_status (src/haute/_git.py:382-388). Prefer `git status --porcelain -z` (NUL-delimited; for rename/copy 'R'/'C' codes git emits the new path then the old path as separate NUL fields) and take the NEW path.
